events.continuity_hook: Continues the Cedar Rapids short-notice episode after the initial booking, with a carrier time change cutting into his arrival cushion.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the keep-or-change flight options, confirm arrival logistics, and preserve a window seat if the itinerary changes.
events.scenario_brief: A carrier time change moves Jonah's Bay Area outbound to Cedar Rapids thirty-five minutes later, leaving less cushion before his evening demo-materials prep. He needs to compare keeping the current one-connection itinerary against moving to an earlier routing through a different hub. The hotel is already held near the industrial park, but arrival time now needs to be checked against rental-car desk hours and the room notes for coffee maker and mini-fridge. The open question is whether the added fare is worth the safer arrival window.

events.continuity_hook: Returns to the Seattle conference plan once the organizer posts final move-in details, after the urgent Iowa trip is under control.
events.interaction_goal: Lock the Seattle flight and hotel, keeping the booth setup and teardown schedule protected while avoiding the high official-block rate.
events.scenario_brief: The Seattle conference organizer posts final booth move-in details: Jonah must be at the convention center by 1 p.m. Sunday and can leave after Wednesday 4 p.m. teardown. The nearby non-block hotel he liked still has a lower cancellable rate than the official block, but the booking deadline is approaching. A United schedule works, while another carrier has a cleaner Wednesday return. The remaining choices are hotel cancellation terms, carrier timing, and seat selection if the seat map is limited.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new client-site episode after the conference and short-notice training planning, moving back to an industrial plant visit.
events.interaction_goal: Build a flight-and-hotel shortlist that balances Monday arrival timing, hotel location near the plant, and the possibility of extending the stay.
events.scenario_brief: Jonah starts planning a two-night visit to a food-and-beverage plant in Chandler, Arizona. The plant walkthrough is Tuesday at 8 a.m., with a distributor dinner Monday evening, so a Monday after-lunch Bay Area departure is workable only if it gets him to Phoenix without rushing. SFO is easiest, Oakland is acceptable, and a nonstop to PHX is likely. He wants a hotel in Chandler or Tempe rather than downtown Phoenix, with good guest ratings, parking, practical room basics, and nearby dinner options. It is not yet clear whether he will need extra time Wednesday for pump-skid photos.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the Chandler episode after the client adds another meeting and a second-site visit.
events.interaction_goal: Update the Chandler plan for a three-night stay, decide whether one hotel still makes sense, and narrow the Thursday return flight.
events.scenario_brief: The Chandler client adds a Wednesday afternoon controls meeting and asks Jonah to visit a second plant near Mesa on Thursday morning. That pushes the return to Thursday afternoon or evening and raises a hotel-location choice: keep one Chandler hotel for all three nights or move closer to Mesa for the last night. He would rather avoid switching hotels unless the morning drive is clearly worse. Flight options now differ mainly by Thursday departure time and traffic cushion to PHX.

events.continuity_hook: Completes the Chandler episode once the three-night plan is approved.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the Chandler flight and hotel booking details, capture seat and room requests, and prepare a concise trip summary for forwarding.
events.scenario_brief: Jonah gets approval for the added Chandler night and is ready to book. The selected plan is a Monday early-afternoon nonstop into PHX, a Thursday mid-afternoon return after the Mesa visit, and a well-rated Chandler hotel that keeps both plant drives manageable. He wants the reservation notes to request a room with coffee maker and mini-fridge, and he wants a window seat if one is still open. The only loose end is sending arrival details to the distributor and the client security desk.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a lighter personal trip after several work-heavy sessions.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the two flight approaches and a small set of Santa Fe hotel options, with the trade-offs centered on drive time, connection reliability, walkability, and cancellation terms.
events.scenario_brief: After several work trips, Jonah and his spouse start planning a long weekend in Santa Fe for late spring. They can leave the Bay Area Friday after lunch and return Monday, and they want to compare flying nonstop to Albuquerque with a rental-car drive against connecting into Santa Fe with less driving but more schedule risk. The hotel should be around the Plaza or Railyard area, with good guest ratings and walkable restaurant options. Room work-trip basics matter less here, and seating needs to keep the two of them together. The open choice is whether to spend more for a historic inn or choose a simpler hotel with better cancellation terms.
